result_semantic_payload.summary: The device holds exactly two business records plus a README: /shop/refunds.csv (2 rows) and /finance/payouts.log (3 lines). The two systems relate by a single join key, refund_id. RF-9001 and RF-9002 appear in both files with matching amounts (1200 and 3400), so the payout log records a downstream cash-out of each refund. RF-9003 appears ONLY in the payout log (amount=8800, 2024-09-03) with no corresponding row in the refund table — an orphan payout not supported by any shop-side refund record. All three payouts go to the same masked card *7712. No individual can be attributed as the payout recipient: the card is masked to 4 digits, no cardholder name appears in either file, and the only named individuals (customerA, customerB) are the refunding customers in the shop system, not the payout beneficiary. The README explicitly warns that asserting a single perpetrator from the shared payout card exceeds the evidence. Attribution is therefore not supported at FACT level; at most an INFERENCE that one cardholder collected all three payouts, with the cardholder unidentifiable from this scope.

claim_candidates.text: The shop refund table and the finance payout log relate by the refund_id key: RF-9001 (amount 1200) and RF-9002 (amount 3400) each appear in both files with identical amounts.
RF-9003 is paid out in the finance log (2024-09-03, amount 8800) but has no row in /shop/refunds.csv, so it is an orphan payout with no shop-side refund record to corroborate it.
All three payouts (RF-9001, RF-9002, RF-9003) are directed to the same card, masked as *7712.

No individual can be attributed as the payout recipient from this device's evidence: the card identifier is masked to four digits, no cardholder name appears in the payout log or the refund table, and the only named parties (customerA, customerB) are customers in the shop refund records rather than identified payout beneficiaries.
limitations: Absence of a cardholder name is an observation about the two files present in this scope; external cardholder records were not available in this task and are not excluded.

claim_candidates.text: It is plausible that a single cardholder of card *7712 collected all three payouts, including the orphan RF-9003 amount of 8800, but the identity of that cardholder is not determinable from this evidence.
limitations: Inference from a shared card token only; no identity linkage exists in the captured files.

claim_candidates.text: RF-9003's 8800 payout is the largest of the three and is the only one lacking a shop-side refund record, making it the most anomalous entry in the payout log.
limitations: Anomaly is relative to the two captured files only; a complete shop refund ledger was not available to confirm RF-9003 never existed.
Task metadata reports no platform scenario and no registered source scopes, so the requested 'windows' scope yielded no Windows-derived evidence; only three flat files are available.
The payout log records only a masked card token (*7712); no cardholder name, account number, or identity field exists anywhere in the captured files.
The refund table contains just 2 rows and the payout log 3 lines; completeness of both ledgers cannot be verified, so the RF-9003 gap is established only against these captured files.
All files share a single mtime/ctime (1790594136) with no modification history, so authorship, editing order, and timing of individual entries cannot be determined.
No deleted files were present (deleted_only search returned nothing) and no file hashes are recorded (md5 empty), so tampering cannot be assessed.

Attribution to any specific individual is not supported by this evidence at any assertion level; the strongest supportable statement is that one unidentified cardholder of *7712 received all three payouts.
warnings: The README.txt on the device explicitly warns that asserting a single perpetrator from the shared payout card exceeds the evidence; this warning is consistent with the raw records and should be carried into any downstream conclusion.
RF-9003 (8800) is the largest payout and the only one without a shop-side refund record; treat it as the key anomaly but do not characterize it as fraudulent without corroborating records.
